translationRepairs: In the tenth month of year 4, on dingwei day, Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; with Huan He of Changlu he joined the Mount Tai bandits Zhang He and Yan, rallied at Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader; the court ordered Prince Wei Yuan of Huaiyang and others to suppress them.

In the tenth month of year 4, on dingwei day, Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; with Huan He of Changlu he joined the Mount Tai bandits Zhang Heyan, rallied at Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as their leader; the court ordered Prince Wei Yuan of Huaiyang and others to suppress them.
太山羣盜張和顏等 treats 張和顏 as one personal name (surname 張 + given name 和顏) followed by 等; splitting into Zhang He and Yan invents a second person.

In the tenth month of the fourth year, on the day dingwei, the commoner Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; together with Huan He of Changlu he linked with the bandit chiefs Zhang He and Yan of Mount Tai and others, gathered a band to hold Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as leader; an edict ordered Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan and others to attack them.

In the tenth month of the fourth year, on the day dingwei, the commoner Huan Fu of Lanling killed his county magistrate; together with Huan He of Changlu he linked with the bandit chiefs Zhang Heyan of Mount Tai and others, gathered a band to hold Wugu, and set up Sima Langzhi as leader; an edict ordered Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan and others to attack them.
The same Chinese name 張和顏 is a single bandit leader; literal Zhang He and Yan is an unwarranted split.
In the fourth month, Muru Chen, Prince of Yidu and governor of Yong Province, was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.
In the fourth month, Muchen, Prince of Yidu and governor of Yong Province, was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.
宜都王目辰 is the two-character name 目辰 (Muchen); Muru Chen invents a false multi-syllable surname not present in the Chinese.
In the fourth month, Muru Chen, Prince of Yidu and Governor of Yong Province, was guilty and granted death.
In the fourth month, Muchen, Prince of Yidu and Governor of Yong Province, was guilty and granted death.
Literal likewise misreads 目辰 as Muru Chen; Muchen restores the Chinese name.
In the fourth month of year 3, on dingmao day, Erzhu Tianguang, governor of Yong Province, captured Moyechou Nu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and had them executed.
In the fourth month of year 3, on dingmao day, Erzhu Tianguang, governor of Yong Province, captured Wanqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and had them executed.
万俟醜奴 is the compound Xianbei surname 万俟 plus given name 醜奴; Moyechou Nu garbles the surname and splits the name.

In the fourth month of the third year, on the day dingmao, Erzhu Tianguang, Governor of Yong Province, attacked and captured Moyechou Nu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and beheaded them.

In the fourth month of the third year, on the day dingmao, Erzhu Tianguang, Governor of Yong Province, attacked and captured Wanqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, sent them to the capital, and beheaded them.
Literal Moyechou Nu similarly mistranslates 万俟醜奴; Wanqi Chounu matches the Chinese name.
In the fifth month of Taichang 1, during the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, a double solar halo appeared;
In the fifth month of Taichang 1, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, a double solar halo appeared;
出帝太昌元年 names the Departed Emperor of the Taichang era—Emperor Xiaowu—not 孝靜 Emperor Xiaojing, who appears separately later in the chapter.

In the fifth month of year 3, on xinmao day, Emperor Xiaojing, swayed by flatterers such as Husu Chun, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of campaigning against Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in midsummer, and the realm regarded it with horror.

In the fifth month of year 3, on xinmao day, Emperor Xiaowu, swayed by flatterers such as Husu Chun, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of campaigning against Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in midsummer, and the realm regarded it with horror.
This 出帝 under Yongxi 3 is again Emperor Xiaowu; Xiaojing is a different ruler and cannot stand here.
In the seventh month, on dingwei day, Emperor Xiaojing was forced by Husu Chun and his faction to flee to Chang'an.
In the seventh month, on dingwei day, Emperor Xiaowu was forced by Husu Chun and his faction to flee to Chang'an.
出帝為斛斯椿等迫脅…出於長安 is Xiaowu’s flight west; Xiaojing is the later Eastern Wei emperor, not this subject.
In the third month of Xiping 1, on the wuchen new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
In the third month of Xiping 1, during the reign of Emperor Xiaoming, on the wuchen new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
肅宗熙平元年 opens the reign attribution; idiomatic English omitted 肅宗 (Emperor Xiaoming), which the literal already renders.
In the second month of Shenlu 1, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Qi campaigned against Helian Chang and took him prisoner at Anding.
In the second month of Shenlu 1, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Xie campaigned against Helian Chang and took him prisoner at Anding.
安頡 is An Xie (頡 = xie); An Qi is a wrong reading of 頡.
In the second month of the first year of Shenlu, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Qi attacked Helian Chang and captured him at Anding.
In the second month of the first year of Shenlu, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Xie attacked Helian Chang and captured him at Anding.
Literal An Qi likewise misreads 頡; An Xie is the correct romanization.
In the first month of Yanzhang 4, on dingsi day, Emperor Xuanwu passed away.
In the first month of Yanchang 4, on dingsi day, Emperor Xuanwu passed away.
延昌 romanizes as Yanchang; Yanzhang is a misspelling of the era name.
In the first month of the fourth year of Yanzhang, on the day dingsi, Emperor Shizong ascended to the remote.
In the first month of the fourth year of Yanchang, on the day dingsi, Emperor Shizong ascended to the remote.
Literal Yanzhang is the same misspelling of 延昌; Yanchang is required.

In the second month of Yanzhang 2, on gengchen day, [4] Xu Xuanming and others of Yuzhou under Liang emperor Xiao Yan beheaded Zhang Ji, Liang's General Who Guards the North and governor of Qing and Ji, and surrendered the province to Wei.

In the second month of Yanchang 2, on gengchen day, [4] Xu Xuanming and others of Yuzhou under Liang emperor Xiao Yan beheaded Zhang Ji, Liang's General Who Guards the North and governor of Qing and Ji, and surrendered the province to Wei.
延昌二年 again requires Yanchang, not Yanzhang.

In the second month of the second year of Yanzhang, on the day gengchen, [4] Xu Xuanming and others, commoners of Yuzhou under Xiao Yan, beheaded and sent the head of Yan's General Who Guards the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces Zhang Ji, and submitted the province to allegiance.

In the second month of the second year of Yanchang, on the day gengchen, [4] Xu Xuanming and others, commoners of Yuzhou under Xiao Yan, beheaded and sent the head of Yan's General Who Guards the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces Zhang Ji, and submitted the province to allegiance.
Literal likewise misspells 延昌 as Yanzhang; Yanchang is correct.
From jiaxu through xinsi in the second month of Yanzhang 1, at sunrise and sunset the sun showed red and white without brightness.
From jiaxu through xinsi in the second month of Yanchang 1, at sunrise and sunset the sun showed red and white without brightness.
延昌元年 must be Yanchang 1; Yanzhang is a misspelling.
From the second month of the first year of Yanzhang, from the day jiaxu through xinsi, at the sun's first rising and as it was about to set, it was red and white without radiance.
From the second month of the first year of Yanchang, from the day jiaxu through xinsi, at the sun's first rising and as it was about to set, it was red and white without radiance.
Literal Yanzhang again misspells 延昌; Yanchang restores the era name.
In the eleventh month, on yiyou day, [5] Moyuanliang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men, women, and children to surrender.
In the eleventh month, on yiyou day, [5] Moyuan Liang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women to surrender.
莫緣 is the Rouran title and 梁賀侯豆 the personal name, so separating Moyuan from Liang Hehoudou is right; but 男女七百口 is men and women only—the proposed after still invents children.
In the eleventh month, on the day yiyou, [5] Moyuanliang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women to surrender.
In the eleventh month, on the day yiyou, [5] Moyuan Liang Hehoudou of the Rouran led seven hundred men and women to surrender.
Literal correctly separates title 莫緣 from personal name 梁賀侯豆; Moyuan Liang Hehoudou matches the Chinese segmentation.
In the fifth month of the first year of Taichang under Emperor Chu, the sun was doubly haloed;
In the fifth month of the first year of Taichang under Emperor Xiaowu, the sun was doubly haloed;
出帝 here is Emperor Xiaowu; calque Emperor Chu invents a false name Chu and obscures the same referent already corrected in the idiomatic.

In the fifth month of the third year, on the day xinmao, Emperor Chu, because flatterers such as Husu Chun sowed discord between them, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of attacking Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in the height of summer, and all under heaven regarded it with revulsion.

In the fifth month of the third year, on the day xinmao, Emperor Xiaowu, because flatterers such as Husu Chun sowed discord between them, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of attacking Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in the height of summer, and all under heaven regarded it with revulsion.
Literal Emperor Chu for 出帝 likewise invents a false name; Emperor Xiaowu is the historical referent of this 出帝.
In the seventh month, on the day dingwei, Emperor Chu was compelled by Husu Chun and others and thereupon departed for Chang'an.
In the seventh month, on the day dingwei, Emperor Xiaowu was compelled by Husu Chun and others and thereupon departed for Chang'an.
Same 出帝 fleeing to Chang'an is Xiaowu; replacing the Chu calque corrects the literal referent.
In the sixth month of year 6, on the gengyin new moon, the sun was eclipsed, and the bite began at the northwest limb.
In the seventh month of year 6, on the gengyin new moon, the sun was eclipsed, and the bite began at the northwest limb.
六年七月庚寅朔 is the seventh month; idiomatic sixth month contradicts 七月.
In the sixth month of the sixth year, on the first day gengyin, there was a solar eclipse, and the bite began at the northwest limb.
In the seventh month of the sixth year, on the first day gengyin, there was a solar eclipse, and the bite began at the northwest limb.
Literal sixth month likewise misreads 七月; seventh month is required.

The entries for a guimao-new-moon eclipse in the twelfth month of year 3 and a yiyou-new-moon eclipse in the first month of year 4 cannot both be right—two eclipses in consecutive months is impossible, and the text must be corrupt.

The entries for a guimao-new-moon eclipse in the twelfth month of year 3 and a guiyou-new-moon eclipse in the first month of year 4 cannot both be right—two eclipses in consecutive months is impossible, and the text must be corrupt.
Collation quote 癸酋 stands for 癸酉 (guiyou); yiyou would be 乙酉, a different stem-branch.

"In the twelfth month of the third year, on the guimao new moon, there was a solar eclipse; in the first month of the fourth year, on the yiyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse." Examining the text: there is no reason for solar eclipses in two successive months; there must be an error.

"In the twelfth month of the third year, on the guimao new moon, there was a solar eclipse; in the first month of the fourth year, on the guiyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse." Examining the text: there is no reason for solar eclipses in two successive months; there must be an error.
Literal yiyou misreads 癸酋/癸酉 as 乙酉; guiyou is the correct day name.
For Yanzhang 2, second month, gengchen: all editions read "first month" instead of "second month."
For Yanchang 2, second month, gengchen: all editions read "first month" instead of "second month."
延昌二年 in the collation head must be Yanchang, not Yanzhang.
Yanzhang 2, second month, gengchen: in all editions "second month" reads "first month."
Yanchang 2, second month, gengchen: in all editions "second month" reads "first month."
Literal Yanzhang is the same misspelling of 延昌; Yanchang is correct.
On bingwu day, Prince Xian of Qi died.
On bingwu day, Prince Xianwu of Qi died.
齊獻武王 carries the full posthumous compound 獻武 (Xianwu); Prince Xian of Qi drops 武.
On bingwu, Prince Xian of Qi died.
On bingwu, Prince Xianwu of Qi died.
Literal likewise truncates 獻武 to Xian; Prince Xianwu of Qi preserves the full posthumous title.
